messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 — High tail latency for customer Sombrero (single-tenant). p99 gen latency spike (18s) and streaming stalls reported. Pager: anna_oncall.

anna_oncall: oncall here, acknowledged. Pulling graphs and logs. tagging @ryan_eng @maria_sre for runtime/kv cache checks.

ryan_eng: seeing large p99 jump starting 2026-03-15T10:14Z. Top of stack shows streaming sessions stuck at `send_chunk` for 15-20s. Worker cpu and GPU utilization normal but kube events show frequent pod restarts on node gpu-node-7.

maria_sre: logs show a lot of very long, multipart prompts (embedded JSON arrays) from Sombrero. These look like repeated preambles causing huge KV prefix growth and rapid evictions. Example prompt snippet (redacted):
```
{"user_message": "... (long JSON with repeated system instructions, ~14k chars)"}
```
This would blow the KV cache and cause tail stalls on streaming when KV misses happen.

joseph_sombrero-sre: we didn't deploy anything recently on our side. Traffic pattern changed — customers running batch import + interactive chat concurrently. We're seeing lots of concurrent sessions from a single org key.

anna_oncall: quick impact summary for executives: affected sessions ~120 concurrent from Sombrero, p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~18s, streaming error spike ~12%. Customer-facing: degraded streaming responsiveness, intermittent partial responses.

ryan_eng: immediate mitigations I'm proposing: 1) route Sombrero to a lower-latency model variant (quantized slim) as temporary fallback, 2) increase dedicated pool capacity for that tenant, 3) disable client-side streaming for new sessions (force non-streaming) to reduce chunking stalls.

maria_sre: agree. Also bump KV cache limit for sessions tagged with somb_org_id to reduce eviction churn. Will patch runtime config now.

anna_oncall: doing step 1 — applying routing change to fallback variant. Executing rollout via console API.

infra-bot: autoscale triggered: scaled dedicated pool somb-pool from 4 -> 8 GPUs. New nodes provisioning. kubectl logs shows pods scheduling to gpu-node-9/10.

anna_oncall: curl to change route (running):
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood/api/v1/routes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"customer":"sombrero","route":"variant","value":"gptx-ffn-slim-quant"}'
```
Response: 202 accepted. Rolling out traffic shift (canary 10% -> 100% in 90s).

maria_sre: patching runtime KV config: increasing per-tenant KV-max-prefixes from 256 -> 1024 for somb_org_id. Restarting runtime workers gracefully.

ryan_eng: temporarily disabling streaming on edge for new sessions from somb_org_id (flagging request header x-disable-streaming: true). Patch pushed to edge-proxy; will monitor.

maria_sre: metrics after routing & kv patch (10:21Z):
```
p95: 1.2s -> 1.1s
p99: 18.3s -> 1.8s
streaming_error_rate: 12% -> 1.5%
kv_evictions/s: 420 -> 38
```
Looks much better post-mitigation.

joseph_sombrero-sre: thanks, seeing improved UX on our side. streaming still disabled for a subset; re-enabling gradually would be good after confirming stability.

anna_oncall: creating follow-up INC ticket INC-9876 with remediation actions: longer-term: rate-limit multi-part prompts, add prompt-size cutoff for single-tenant burst detection, improve autoscale headroom.

ryan_eng: next investigative items: correlate exact prompt patterns -> which client library/version, check if a frontend batching change caused repeated preamble, and review node gpu-node-7 OOM/restart reason.

maria_sre: log excerpt from runtime showing eviction storms and prefix blowup: 
```
2026-03-15T10:14:03Z runtime WARN kv_cache: tenant=somb_org_id prefix_count=1123 evictions=87 reason=prefix_exceeded
2026-03-15T10:14:04Z runtime WARN stream: session=abc123 stalled at send_chunk (kv_miss)
```

anna_oncall: handoff plan — monitoring for 2h, then hand to night oncall at 2026-03-15T22:00Z if stable. Scheduled follow-up call 11:00Z to review mitigations with @joseph_sombrero-sre.

infra-bot: note: node gpu-node-7 had kernel OOM killer events around 10:13Z, likely due to memory pressure from a rogue pod; cordoned that node temporarily.

ryan_eng: action items assigned:
- @maria_sre: permanent KV policy change + runbook update (INC-9876-1)
- @ryan_eng: root-cause on frontend client + check deploy logs (INC-9876-2)
- @infra-bot: ensure node gpu-node-7 remains cordoned until drain/patch (INC-9876-3)

maria_sre: will also add an alert for per-tenant KV eviction rate > 200/s to trigger autosuggested mitigations.

anna_oncall: marking as mitigated but not resolved. Will keep thread open for handoff. :white_check_mark:
